messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager duty alert for serve-prod-eu: high error rate (503) and injector:container crash loop detected. Pager duty runbook linked: https://runbooks.internal/repro/rdma

tia (oncall): ACK. Investigating. seeing a spike of retransmits on rdma iface and a cascade of CUDA OOMs in the serving sidecars. root logs attached below.

mike (serving): confirming, recent alerts show GPU oom events lined up with IB retransmit bursts. stack traces look like kv-cache miss rebuilds + big batch attempts. sample log:```
[2026-03-15T18:12:04Z] serve: request_id=abcd1234 model=instruct-x batch_size=64 alloc_failed: CUDA out of memory
[2026-03-15T18:12:04Z] runtime: kvcache reload started (prefix miss)
[2026-03-15T18:12:05Z] rdma: retransmit=124 cpu=eth0 mtu=1500 frag=1
```

tia (oncall): Node set show: node-serve-07 and node-serve-08 both reporting 'rdma timeout' and then kubelet kills containers for OOM. Starting mitigation: 1) reduce max_batch to 8 for unstable nodes, 2) cordon+drain node-serve-07/08, 3) set model fallback policy to degrade to cpu-path for critical customers.

anna (sre): Commands I'm running now:```
kubectl cordon node-serve-07 && kubectl drain node-serve-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60
kubectl patch configmap/serve-config -p '{"data":{"max_batch":"8"}}' -n prod
```

raj (netinfra): Seeing a pattern in switch counters: fragmented packets and reassembly fails on leaf-sw-12 where node-serve-07/08 are plugged. Switch shows high 'frag' increment and occasional egress drops. Also saw a recent MTU change applied in rack 12 yesterday 22:30 UTC (from 9216 -> 1500). Can you confirm kernel/firmware changes?

mike (serving): We rolled a kernel firmware update on those nodes at 2026-03-15 22:45 UTC (auto-rolling). Could be MTU mismatch with jumbo disabled on the fabric. That would cause RDMA to fragment, retransmit and exacerbate latency -> uv-kvcache thrash -> OOM.

raj (netinfra): Exact. When RDMA frames fragment into IP fragments on some paths we see reassembly timeouts on the NIC and the RDMA driver raises RNR and RTO which triggers resend storms. I'm going to isolate the leaf port and force link to 9216 to test. If immediate fix is needed we can re-enable jumbo on the switches or rollback the kernel MTU clamp we applied.

tia (oncall): Short mitigation checklist applied: 
- Drain node-serve-07/08 (in progress)
- Patch serve-config to max_batch=8 (done)
- Activate route fallback: set router policy serve-prod-eu -> prefer tcp for model-instruct-x (temporary)
- Notify customers via cs-ops

cs-ops: Noted, informing top 5 affected customers. Early ETA for full restore depends on whether netinfra can re-enable jumbo or we can migrate pods cleanly. Current failure rate ~12% of requests for EU cluster, affecting ~3 paid customers.

anna (sre): drain completed on node-serve-07. Starting pod restarts on healthy nodes. Observed one pod dropped to node-serve-09 and resumed. Error spikes reducing after batch cap and drain.

raj (netinfra): Quick test: toggled MTU back to 9216 on leaf-sw-12 for the two ports, verifying no config drift. Counters show retransmits dropping immediately. I'm rolling the change cluster-wide for rack 12.

mike (serving): After switch MTU change and draining, GPUs reporting stable memory after 4m. No new OOMs in last 3m. Throughput down ~22% because of smaller batches but latency stabilized.

incident-bot: Incident severity set to Sev2. Timeline auto-log created: https://incidents.internal/1968723456

anna (sre): Next steps: keep traffic on fallback TCP route for 15m to monitor. If stable, start gradual re-enable of batch size to 16 then 32. Also capturing heap dump for the pod that crashed for postmortem.

mike (serving): Agree. I will also add a safeguard: if rdma retransmit rate > 5/min for a node, autoscaler should mark node unhealthy and drain automatically. Filing infra ticket.

raj (netinfra): Root cause preliminary: MTU mismatch after rolling kernel change + switch configuration mismatch led to IP fragmentation of RDMA frames -> retransmit storms -> increased latency and repeated kv-cache invalidations -> larger in-flight memory pressure -> CUDA OOMs and container restarts.

tia (oncall): Handoff in 20m to next oncall: @anna you'll be taking follow-up. Please include network infra in postmortem and mitigation plan for future kernel rollouts.

anna (sre): ACK handoff. I'll collect diagnostics: NIC logs, switch counters, kube events, and model eval traces. Targets for postmortem: action items to prevent silent MTU drift, add MTU verification in node rollout playbook, and a guard to autotrim batch sizes under rdma error conditions.

pagerduty-bot: Next oncall: anna (sre) will be on-call from 19:00Z.

cs-ops: Sent customer update at 18:20Z: "We mitigated a serving degradation in EU caused by network fragmentation; traffic restored on fallback path; performance impact reduced; full postmortem will follow."

mike (serving): Logging mitigation notes to runbook: make 'force-tcp-fallback' a one-click action in console, and add 'set-max-batch' to default incident templates.

anna (sre): last checks: no new OOMs for 12m, retransmits back to baseline. Leaving cluster in fallback mode for 30m then will ramp batches. Closing active page if nothing new in 30.

tia (oncall): Thanks team. I'll mark the incident as mitigated pending postmortem. :thumbsup:

-- end of thread --
